post.summary: Block account
post.description:
Block the given account. Clients should filter statuses from this account if received (e.g. due to a boost in the Home timeline).

Unlike Mastodon, Verso tells neither the account nor its instance, and blocking ends no follows.

Needs a token for a user, not one an app got for itself. Needs the `owner:block` permission.

post.summary: Unblock account
post.description:
Unblock the given account.

Needs a token for a user, not one an app got for itself. Needs the `owner:block` permission.

post.summary: Mute account
post.description:
Mute the given account. Clients should filter statuses and notifications from this account, if received (e.g. due to a boost in the Home timeline).

Muting an account already muted changes how it is muted. Durations are at most five years.

Needs a token for a user, not one an app got for itself. Needs the `owner:mute` permission.

notifications.description: Mute notifications in addition to statuses? Defaults to true.

duration.description: How long the mute should last, in seconds. Defaults to 0 (indefinite).

post.summary: Block a domain
post.description:
Block a domain to change interactions with that domain's server.

Unlike Mastodon, Verso tells no one, keeps the viewer's followers there, and lets its users still follow them. Instead, it blocks each account on the domain, and on its subdomains, as blocking the account would. The domain must be a domain name.

Needs a token for a user, not one an app got for itself. Needs the `owner:block` permission.

post.summary: Upload media as an attachment (async)
post.description:
Creates a media attachment to be used with a new status. The full sized media will be processed asynchronously in the background for large uploads.

Pictures are processed, and answered with 202 until they are; any other file is kept as it is, as a file of type `unknown`. A picture that can't be processed is removed, as it may hold metadata, and then answered with 422. Files are at most 16777216 bytes.

Needs a token for a user, not one an app got for itself. Needs the `owner:media` permission.
